title: A Compass for the Letter
premise: In 1890s port city of Corvane, Tamsin Okafor, a pearl diver's son indentured to the Meridian Trading Company, has learned to survive by carrying only what can be lifted and left behind. When he is ordered to deliver a sealed letter to a dying shipwright, he discovers it names him as heir to the man's workshop — and entangles him in a company scheme to burn the yard for insurance before a debt-laden ship sails. With found family among the shipwright's ragtag apprentices, Tamsin must finish the vessel's repairs, expose the plot, and choose between the freedom of carrying nothing and the weight of belonging. He stays through the fire, saves the workshop, and signs his own name to the deed as the ship sails on the morning tide.
about_author: Sable Nystrom is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent years cataloguing indenture ledgers from colonial trading ports. Their fiction explores the paper trails that bind people to places they never chose.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. We meet him inventorying cargo at Meridian Trading, measuring his life in portable things: a mother's pearl, a diver's knife, no surname he trusts. The company clerk hands him a sealed letter with orders to deliver it personally. Emotional beat: quiet resignation cracked by first curiosity.

chapters.title: The Dying Hand
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He delivers the letter to old Bramwen Hale, a shipwright coughing blood in a sagging yard. Hale reads it, laughs, and tells Tamsin the letter names him heir — but only if the workshop still stands when the ship Kestrel sails. Emotional beat: disbelief hardening into wary hope.

chapters.title: Apprentices of Sawdust
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, with interludes from apprentice Wren. The yard's misfits — Wren, deaf caulkers, a disgraced navigator — test then slowly accept him. He learns the Kestrel is unseaworthy and the deadline impossible. Emotional beat: the unfamiliar warmth of being needed.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren discovers Meridian has insured the Kestrel for triple its worth and scheduled her maiden voyage impossibly soon. Tamsin realizes the company expects the ship — and the yard — to fail catastrophically. Emotional beat: dread replacing gratitude; the letter was bait.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Name
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He confronts the clerk who gave him the letter, learning Hale chose him deliberately — a diver's son who could read water and wood alike. Flashback to his mother's drowning. Emotional beat: grief surfacing, identity questioned: was he chosen or used?

chapters.title: Night Work
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation. The crew works by lamplight to make the Kestrel seaworthy while saboteurs loosen planking at night. Tamsin catches a Meridian man mid-sabotage and lets him go to follow him back to his paymaster. Emotional beat: resolve sharpening into strategy.

chapters.title: The Paymaster's Offer
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The company offers him his indenture papers, free and clear, if he walks away and lets the fire happen. Alone with everything he owns in one bag, he almost takes it. Emotional beat: the seduction of weightlessness versus the terror of staying.

chapters.title: Fire on the Slipway
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Climax begins: hired men torch the yard early. Tamsin leads the apprentices fighting the flames, Wren nearly dies saving the deed chest, and Tamsin uses a diver's breath-hold to reach the burning underhull and cut the Kestrel loose into deep water where she can't spread fire. Emotional beat: sacrifice without guarantee.

chapters.title: Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Scorched but standing, the yard watches the repaired Kestrel sail safely past the harbor bar, disproving Meridian's 'accident' narrative. Harbor witnesses and a sympathetic customs officer turn against the company. Emotional beat: exhausted triumph, fragile vindication.

chapters.title: A Compass for the Letter
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Meridian collapses under inquiry; Tamsin's indenture is voided. He unpacks his single bag for the first time in years, hanging his mother's pearl above the workbench, and signs the deed with his full name: Tamsin Okafor Hale. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited — home as something carried inward.
